title_candidates: GPT-6 Sol and Luna arrive in ChatGPT Work
Choose between GPT-6 Sol and Luna with one test
summary: OpenAI has added GPT-6 Sol and Luna to ChatGPT Work and Codex. A controlled 15-minute comparison can show which one better fits a repeatable task.

primary_source.title: Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna
primary_source.author: OpenAI
key_facts: OpenAI positions GPT-6 Sol and Luna as faster, less expensive ways to use advances introduced with GPT-6 Astra, while Astra remains its highest-capability option.
OpenAI lists API prices per million tokens at $2 input and $10 output for Sol, and $0.10 input and $0.50 output for Luna; those prices are separate from ChatGPT subscription usage.

On an internal set drawn from conversations in which users flagged factual errors, OpenAI says Sol made about half as many mistakes as GPT-5.6 Sol, while cautioning that the test cases are harder than typical use.
OpenAI reports that both models use a clearer, less verbose communication style derived from Astra.
Sol and Luna are available in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users; Luna is also available to Free and Go users in the desktop app.
The models are not yet available in regular Chat, and OpenAI says rollout through ChatGPT is gradual, so eligible users may not see them immediately.
The API model IDs are gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-luna.

quote_candidates.text: Free and Go users can access GPT-6 Luna in the desktop app. These models are not yet available in Chat.

supporting_sources.title: ChatGPT Work and Codex
key_facts: OpenAI's help page says Sol and Luna are Work and Codex models, not regular Chat models, and that availability depends on plan, workspace settings, and rollout access.
In Work, the model picker can use a Default slider or a specific model with its available reasoning levels.
Work is available on the web and mobile for eligible paid plans and in the desktop app when the user's plan and workspace allow it.

prerequisites: A browser or the latest ChatGPT desktop app
A signed-in Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, or Edu account with Work enabled
GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna visible in the Work model picker

steps.instruction: Open [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com), sign in, and select Work. In the desktop app, select ChatGPT from the top-left menu, then choose Work at the top of the page. Stop if Work is unavailable; managed-workspace access may depend on admin settings.

Start a new Work chat, open the model picker, select GPT-6 Luna, and choose a reasoning level. Paste: 'Fictional event budget: venue $1,250; catering for 37 people at $28 each; transport $360; contingency 10% of the subtotal. Show the arithmetic, give the final total, and summarise it in three bullets.' Record the answer.
Start a fresh Work chat, select GPT-6 Sol, use the same reasoning level if both model menus offer it, and paste the identical prompt. Record the answer without giving Sol Luna's result.

Check both answers independently: catering is $1,036, the subtotal is $2,646, contingency is $264.60, and the final total is $2,910.60. Mark any arithmetic error, missing working, or unsupported change to the invented inputs.

Compare correctness, clarity, and time to the first useful answer. Keep the model that performed better on this exact task. If either model is absent, do not infer its performance; wait for rollout or ask your workspace admin.

risk_flags: Sol and Luna are not available in regular Chat; the article and guide must keep the Work/Codex distinction explicit.
Rollout is gradual and managed-workspace settings can hide the models even on an eligible plan.
API token prices must not be presented as ChatGPT subscription prices.
The practical guide is an original controlled comparison, not a benchmark of general model quality.
